output.title: Typical wait time for a member callback
output.draft_text:
Question: How long does a member usually wait for a callback?

Answer: After a callback is requested, a member can usually expect a call back within [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or business days]. Callbacks are made during [callback hours of operation and time zone]. If the request is submitted after [daily cutoff time] or on a [weekend/holiday], the timeframe begins on the next [business day].

Wait times may be longer when [conditions that extend wait times, e.g., peak enrollment periods or high call volume]. During these periods, the expected wait is [extended timeframe, if any].

For urgent issues, [priority/escalation path for urgent requests, if one exists] applies, with a callback expected within [urgent callback timeframe].

The callback will come from [phone number or caller ID the member will see]. If the member misses the call, [number of callback attempts] attempts will be made, and [what happens after missed attempts, e.g., voicemail left or the request is closed].

If the member has not received a callback within [timeframe after which to follow up], they should [follow-up steps, e.g., call the main line at [phone number] and reference their request number].
placeholders: [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or business days]
[callback hours of operation and time zone]
[conditions that extend wait times, e.g., peak enrollment periods or high call volume]
[priority/escalation path for urgent requests, if one exists]
[phone number or caller ID the member will see]
[what happens after missed attempts, e.g., voicemail left or the request is closed]
[follow-up steps, e.g., call the main line at [phone number] and reference their request number]
author_checklist: Confirm which callback program this covers (general member services, benefits, pharmacy, claims, etc.) and whether timeframes differ by team or request type.
Confirm the official standard callback timeframe and whether it is a service-level commitment or only a typical estimate.
Confirm whether timeframes are counted in business hours, business days, or calendar days.
Confirm callback hours of operation, time zone, and daily cutoff time.
Confirm whether wait times change during peak periods (e.g., open enrollment) and what extended timeframe, if any, should be communicated.
Confirm whether an urgent or priority callback path exists, who qualifies, and its timeframe. Remove that paragraph if no such path exists.
Confirm the phone number or caller ID members will see.
Confirm the number of callback attempts and what happens after missed attempts.
Confirm the follow-up process and contact number if a callback is not received.
Confirm whether any regulatory or contractual response-time requirements apply and should be referenced.
Remove any placeholder sections that do not apply before submitting for approval.
Choose the correct knowledge base: benefits is suggested, but move it to pharmacy if this applies to pharmacy callbacks.
